To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the proposed DASNet architecture achieves competitive results with a small set of mask annotations; (2) the detection module is able to learn a good initialization for the segmentation module, which is crucial to reduce the required mask annotations.
we propose a new semi-supervised instance and semantic segmentation approach that is based on a detection network and that we demonstrate that it achieves state-of-the-art performance.

(a) we can achieve state-of-the-art instance and semantic segmentation performance with a small set of mask annotations and a much larger set of box annotations; (b) the detection module in our network can be replaced by any detection model that is able to generate class specific features; and (c) the proposed attention module is able to generate multi-scale features and is effective to improve performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: 1.
the problem of reducing the amount of expensive human annotation efforts in pixel-level segmentation tasks, while maintaining high performance.
the problem of reducing pixel-level annotations for instance and semantic segmentation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method achieves high quality instance and segmentation results over a limited set of mask annotations and a much larger set of box annotations.
our work is the first to show how to use a large set of bounding box annotations to improve pixel-level semantic segmentation.
the proposed approach achieves high quality instance and segmentation results over a large number of box annotations and a small set of mask annotations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can obtain state-of-the-art performance for both instance and semantic segmentation tasks using only a fraction of pixel-level annotations.

(i) DASNet achieves competitive results compared to supervised methods using only 10% of the original mask annotation, (ii) DASNet outperforms existing semi-supervised methods using only 20% of the mask annotation.
we can achieve state-of-the-art performance for instance segmentation using only 1.6% pixel-level annotations and 98.4% box-level annotations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the detection model can be used as a bridge to reduce the amount of pixel-level annotations and thus to improve the performance of deep segmentation networks.
detection models can be used to simplify the pixel-wise supervised learning task.
the performance of deep learning models can be significantly improved by leveraging a large number of box annotations.
